subject: research/accel-nsgatune
professional: a researcher in evolutionary multi-objective optimisation applied to hardware design-space exploration (the kind who reviews for IEEE TEVC, GECCO/EMO or DAC/ICCAD DSE tracks). They would check first that the NSGA-II is the Deb et al. (2002) algorithm, that the quality indicator and its reference point are meaningful, that differences between settings are tested with the right statistic (standard error / Wilcoxon over seeds, not raw seed sd), that tuning is not reported on the same seeds it was chosen on, and whether a hyperparameter sweep on an enumerable 3,840-point space with one budget and only a random-search baseline says anything new against the parameter-tuning (irace, Smit and Eiben) and DSE (Bayesian optimisation, HyperMapper) literature.

evidence.correctness: Ran `cd research/accel-nsgatune && time python3 experiments/run.py` (2 min 08 s wall, under load from two other jobs): results.json and results.txt rewritten byte-identical (`git status --short` empty afterwards); `python3 experiments/figure.py` rewrote mutation_sweep.svg with no diff. Independent recomputation in a scratch script (scratchpad/indep.py, run with `python3 -I`, does NOT import accel_nsga or accel_nsgatune): own evaluation model re-derived from accel-nsga's README text and the raw accel-kws / accel-codesign JSON, own constrained-domination filter, own exact hypervolume by coordinate-compressed grid (not the subject's slicing algorithm), own textbook NSGA-II (Deb 2002 fast non-dominated sort with domination counts, crowding distance, crowded binary tournament on (rank, -crowding), (mu+lambda) replacement, uniform crossover, per-gene mutation, duplicates free against the unique-design budget). Results: (1) feasible designs 2,608 (50 us) and 3,632 (200 us), exact fronts 41 and 33 distinct vectors: match accel-nsga README exactly. (2) Random search with the subject's seed scheme (Random(1000*s+400).sample over the same gene order): share 0.129+-0.044 and 0.116+-0.052, HV ratio 0.992 and 0.996: exact match to results.txt via an independent HV algorithm. (3) My NSGA-II on my own seeds (777000+s): pop 20 mut 0.25 gives 0.273 / 0.560 vs reported 0.282 / 0.587; pop 10 mut 0.02 gives 0.423 / 0.762 vs 0.398 / 0.773; pop 10 mut 0.05 0.398 / 0.764 vs 0.399 / 0.759; mutation-only pop 20 mut 0.02 0.421 / 0.729 vs 0.450 / 0.731; pop 80 mut 0.5 0.137 / 0.201 vs 0.132 / 0.185. All within about 1.5 standard errors (SE of a 30-seed mean about 0.012-0.018). Also re-ran the subject's own code on held-out seeds 30-59 (scratchpad/diag.py): pop 10 mut 0.02 0.399 / 0.738, pop 20 mut 0.25 0.284 / 0.541, mutation-only pop 20 mut 0.02 0.432 / 0.730, so the tuned-on-same-seeds optimism is small (0 to 0.05). Only 1 of 30 runs (pop 10 mut 0.02, 50 us) stops short of 400 designs via the stale<200 rule. Numbers are right; capped at 3 because every number sits on accel-nsga's assumed hardware model, which I re-implemented from its own description rather than checked against a measurement.

evidence.verification: Test command: `cd research/accel-nsgatune && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 4 tests, OK, 0.049 s. Five hand-seeded mutations in src/accel_nsgatune/tune.py (each restored from a backup copy, `cmp` confirmed identical, `git status --short` clean afterwards): (M1) disable the crossover switch, `(not crossover or rng.random() < 0.5)` -> `(False or rng.random() < 0.5)`, so the 'no-crossover' variant silently does crossover: NOT caught (4 OK). (M2) tournament min -> max: caught. (M3) mutation `< mut` -> `> mut`: caught. (M4) mutation-only child copies b instead of a: caught (only because it also changes the crossover path's RNG pairing). (M5) budget check `<` -> `<=`: caught. 4 of 5 caught, but the one that survived is the only new behaviour in this project: no test checks that crossover=False actually removes recombination (test_no_crossover_child_is_copy_when_no_mutation only asserts len(items) >= 10, which its name does not describe). The scoring path in run.py (score(), reference point, front-share denominator) has no test; the only behavioural test is equality of the crossover=True path with accel-nsga's nsga2, i.e. a copy checked against its original.
evidence.craft: Read tune.py (30 lines), tests/test_tune.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py, and accel-nsga/src/accel_nsga/search.py (176 lines, the imported engine). Defects: (1) nsga2_x is a copied engine: a line-for-line duplicate of accel_nsga.search.nsga2 with one flag, rather than a parameter added upstream, so the two can drift (the test pins them only on the crossover=True path at one seed); (2) sys.path.insert into a sibling project's src at import time; (3) hard-coded range(4) gene length instead of len(space.dims); (4) tournament uses pop.index(g) as the fitness proxy, O(pop) per comparison, and in the first generation the population is unranked so selection is uniform random there (inherited); (5) a mutation draws rng.randrange(dims[i]), which can return the same value, so the effective per-gene mutation rate is mut*(n_i-1)/n_i and differs by gene (40 vs 4 values), not stated; (6) mutation-only children still draw a and b and consume crossover RNG, harmless but makes RNG streams incomparable across variants; (7) results.json omits per-seed values, so no paired test can be run from the committed artefacts. Readable, deterministic, stdlib only, which is to its credit.
evidence.claims: Every number in the README and page matches results.txt (checked all 7 table rows and each bullet's figures). Stylised status, one budget, one space and tuning on the same seeds are disclosed; AI-assistance note present. Overreaches: (1) README:38 and the page's 'Removing crossover changes little' understate a large effect. Using the stored sd and n=30, the SE of a difference is about 0.02-0.03: at 200 us, pop 40 mut 0.1, crossover 0.663 vs mutation-only 0.486 is z = 6.2; pop 20 mut 0.25, 0.587 vs 0.474 is z = 4.1. The README calls these 'roughly one to two seed sd' and concludes crossover 'helps a little'. Seed sd is the wrong yardstick for a difference of 30-seed means. (2) README:38 says mutation-only is 'level with or slightly ahead ... at every mutation rate' at 50 us; at pop 40 mut 0.05 it is behind (0.328 vs 0.363) and at mut 0.1 (0.307 vs 0.319). (3) README:37 'below about 0.1 the curve is flat (within about one seed sd)': pop 10, 50 us, 0.398 vs 0.359 is about 2 SE; the flatness is asserted with the same misused yardstick. (4) README:39 'only the exact-front share separates the methods': the HV saturation is largely an artefact of the reference point chosen (accuracy 0, area/energy at the space maximum; run.py:26), not a property of the methods. Not fabricated, but the qualitative conclusions on crossover and flatness are not backed by the statistics in the file.
evidence.fitness: Research bar (research/CLAUDE.md: PhD-level programme aimed at a publishable result, deep-tech application). A researcher can reproduce and extend the harness in two minutes, which is useful, but the result is a hyperparameter sweep of a textbook algorithm on a 3,840-design space that is small enough to enumerate (so search is unnecessary), at one budget, with only random search as a baseline. Nearest prior work (from recollection; no outbound literature check was made): Deb et al. (2002) NSGA-II and Deb's standing recommendation of per-variable mutation 1/n (here 1/4 = 0.25, exactly accel-nsga's 'untuned' setting, a link the README does not draw); parameter-tuning of EAs and EMOAs (Eiben and Smit 2011; Lopez-Ibanez et al. irace 2016; Bezerra, Lopez-Ibanez and Stutzle on automatically designed MOEAs); hypervolume indicator and reference-point sensitivity (Zitzler and Thiele 1999; Ishibuchi et al. 2017-2018 on reference-point specification); hardware DSE with NSGA-II and with Bayesian optimisation (e.g. Palermo/Silvano Multicube-style DSE, Nardi et al. HyperMapper 2019, NAAS 2021 cited by the parent). That a small population and low mutation win at a small budget on a tiny discrete space is expected and not new; the crossover question is answered with a misread statistic. No stronger baseline (SMS-EMOA, MOEA/D, MOBO/EHVI, local search), no budget sweep, no generalisation beyond one table. Not a basis for a paper; at most a methods footnote to accel-nsga.
evidence.domain: Compared with EMO experimental practice (e.g. Bartz-Beielstein et al. 2020 'Benchmarking in optimization: best practice'; Knowles, Thiele and Zitzler 2006 tutorial on performance assessment). Matches: Deb constrained domination, crowding, elitist replacement; equal budgets in unique evaluations; many seeds; an exact reference front, which is a genuine strength. Departs: (1) no statistical testing (no Wilcoxon/Mann-Whitney, no multiple-comparison correction across 62 cells, no CIs) and differences judged against seed sd; (2) best settings chosen and reported on the same seeds (disclosed; my held-out check shows the bias is small here, but the practice is wrong); (3) hypervolume reference point at accuracy 0 and space maximum area/energy makes HV insensitive (0.97-0.998 everywhere), so the second indicator is uninformative by construction; a practitioner would use the nadir of the exact front, or IGD+/additive epsilon, or attainment surfaces; (4) mutation rate not expressed per 1/n and the 40-value model gene vs 4-value genes not discussed (mutation is far more disruptive on the model gene); (5) one budget only, though the population result is budget-dependent by construction (pop 80 spends 20% of 400 on initialisation); (6) only a random-search baseline. Sound algorithm, weak experimental design.

defects.what: Crossover conclusion misreads the statistics: differences of 30-seed means are judged against the per-seed sd, so a 0.177 gap (z = 6.2 with SE = sqrt(sd1^2+sd2^2)/sqrt(30)) at 200 us pop 40 mut 0.1 and a 0.113 gap (z = 4.1) at pop 20 mut 0.25 are described as 'roughly one to two seed sd' and the page headline says 'Removing crossover changes little'. Also 'level with or slightly ahead at every mutation rate' at 50 us is false at pop 40 (0.328 vs 0.363, 0.307 vs 0.319).

The only new behaviour (crossover=False) is untested: disabling the switch so the mutation-only variant still recombines leaves all 4 tests passing; test_no_crossover_child_is_copy_when_no_mutation only asserts len(items) >= 10.

Hypervolume reference point at accuracy 0 and the space-maximum area/energy saturates the indicator (0.97-0.998 for every method including random), and the README reports this as a finding ('only the exact-front share separates the methods') rather than a consequence of the reference point.

No significance tests, CIs or multiple-comparison control across 62 cells; 'flat below 0.1' is asserted from seed sd (pop 10, 50 us, 0.02 vs 0.1 is about 2 SE); per-seed values are not stored, so a paired test cannot be run from committed artefacts.
nsga2_x duplicates accel_nsga.search.nsga2 line for line with one flag instead of parametrising the original; hard-coded gene length 4; sys.path import of a sibling project.
accel-nsga's 'untuned' mutation 0.25 is Deb's 1/n default for 4 genes; the README does not say so, and the effective per-gene rate is mut*(n_i-1)/n_i because a mutation can redraw the same value.

verdict: A small, honest, exactly reproducible sweep: run.py rewrote results.json/results.txt byte-identically in 2 min 08 s, and an independent implementation (own evaluation model, own Pareto filter, own grid hypervolume, own textbook Deb 2002 NSGA-II, own seeds) reproduced the feasible counts (2,608 / 3,632), front sizes (41 / 33), random-search share and HV (0.129 / 0.116, 0.992 / 0.996) exactly and the NSGA-II cells to within about 1.5 SE; held-out seeds show the tuned figures are only slightly optimistic. So the numbers are right (correctness 3) and the project does all it says (completeness 3). It does not meet the bar: verification is 2 (the one behaviour the project adds, removing crossover, can be broken without any test failing), claims are 2 (the crossover and 'flat below 0.1' conclusions are read off seed sd instead of standard error, understating a crossover effect of 4-6 SE at 200 us, and HV saturation is reported as a finding when it follows from the reference point), and fitness is 1: tuning a textbook NSGA-II on an enumerable 3,840-point space at one budget against only random search is neither new nor publishable, and the 'untuned' 0.25 was Deb's own 1/n default. Fixes: test the crossover switch, store per-seed values and report paired tests or CIs, rewrite the crossover bullet, use a front-nadir HV reference or IGD+, and add a budget sweep and a stronger baseline.
